The Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan Company (BTC Co) today announced that, effective 1 July 2026, operatorship of the Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan (BTC) oil export pipeline will transfer from bp Exploration (Caspian Sea) Limited (bp) to SOCAR Midstream Operations LLC (SMO), a wholly owned subsidiary of SOCAR, AzerNEWS reports, citing bp.
The transfer applies across all three BTC pipeline sections — Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye. Crude oil exports from Kirkuk to Türkiye’s Mediterranean port of Ceyhan are expected to continue without disruption, despite the expiry of the bilateral agreement governing the Iraq-Türkiye pipeline, as Baghdad and Ankara continue negotiations over a 12-month extension.
Two Turkish sources told Reuters on Thursday that oil flows through the pipeline are likely to remain uninterrupted while discussions continue on a temporary arrangement to maintain exports during negotiations for a new agreement.
The decades-old accord regulating the operation of the Iraq-Türkiye pipeline expired on Monday, 27 July 2026.
One of the sources said the pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational crude export route, will remain in service while both sides work towards an interim agreement to safeguard oil flows until a new framework is finalised.
Neither Türkiye’s Ministry of Energy nor Iraq’s Ministry of Oil has issued an official statement on the pipeline’s status following the expiry of the previous agreement.
Türkiye is seeking to increase utilisation of the pipeline, which has a design capacity of around 1.5 million barrels per day, and is also considering extending it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

The Department of Defense (DOD) broke ground on the Project Pele transportable microreactor project at Idaho National Laboratory (INL).
The demonstration project is being led by DOD’s Strategic Capabilities Office and could be one of the first advanced reactors to operate in the United States as early as 2026.
Project Pele Breaks Ground
DOD is planning to design, build, and demonstrate a transportable high-temperature gas reactor that will operate at the lab’s Critical Infrastructure Test Range Complex.
The reactor will be manufactured by BWX Technologies and connected to INL’s microgrid producing 1 to 5 megawatts of electrical power.
Project Pele is a whole-of-government effort, with critical expertise provided by the Department of Energy, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, NASA, and the National Nuclear Security Administration.
The reactor is expected to operate for a minimum of three years at the lab and will help demonstrate the use of clean, reliable, and transportable nuclear power to help meet the increasing energy demands at military bases across the country.
